title: Dynamic Programming

views.title: Linear DP & State Machines
views.intro: Every DP here is top-down: name the state, write the choice at that state, set the base case, then memoize. Recursion depth is the length of the state chain, so very long inputs need a bigger thread stack.
table: Count ways or min cost where step i reads a few earlier steps
House robber family: f(i) = take or skip
Max subarray / product: memo the best subarray starting at i
f(day, holding, transactions left), cooldown, fee

files.desc: Climbing stairs, rob, decode ways, max subarray, max product, stock I-IV + cooldown + fee

pitfalls: Recursion depth equals the length of the state chain. Java's default stack holds about 10^4 frames; at n = 10^5 (LC 53, 198 variants, 1425, 1696) it overflows. Run the solve inside a big-stack thread: new Thread(null, r, "solve", 1 << 26), start, join (same as SCC_Bridges_2SAT.runWithBigStack).
Max product needs both max AND min: a negative flips them.
Decode ways: a leading zero kills the one-digit option; 10 and 20 are the only valid two-digit zeros.
Stock with k transactions: if k >= n/2 it degenerates to unlimited.

views.title: Knapsack Family
views.intro: Knapsack memo is f(i, capacity). Each item once: taking item i moves to i + 1. Reusable: taking item i stays at i. For counting, combinations fix the coin order with f(coin index, amount); ordered sequences try every coin from f(amount).
table: f(i, cap): skip, or take and move to i + 1
f(i, cap): take and stay at i, or move on
Partition, target sum, last stone II: f(i, remaining)

files.desc: 0/1, unbounded, bounded, subset sum, partition, target sum, coin change min/ways, combination sum IV, perfect squares, ones and zeroes

pitfalls: In a 0/1 problem, taking an item must move to i + 1; staying at i silently reuses it.
Coin Change II (combinations) memoizes f(coin index, amount); Combination Sum IV (sequences) memoizes f(amount) and tries every coin.
Target Sum: the reduction is subsets summing to (total + target) / 2; check parity and range first.

views.title: Sequences & Strings
views.intro: Two sequences give a memo over (i, j) suffixes. One sequence with a pairwise condition gives LIS-style take/skip memo. Palindromes use an interval memo f(i, j).
table: f(i) = 1 + best f(j) over j > i with a[j] > a[i]
f(i, j) over the two suffixes
Wildcard, regex, interleave, distinct subsequences: f(i, j)

files.desc: LIS, count of LIS, envelopes, LCS, edit distance, palindromes, distinct subsequences, word break, wildcard, regex, interleave

pitfalls: Russian Doll: sort width ascending and height DESCENDING so equal widths cannot chain.
Subsequence means order kept, substring means contiguous: contiguous resets to 0 on mismatch.
Regex star: zero copies is f(i, j + 2); one more copy needs the current char to match, then f(i + 1, j).

views.title: Grid & Interval DP
views.intro: Grids memoize f(r, c) over the moves left (dungeon-style answers depend on what comes AFTER, which is the natural top-down direction). Interval memo f(i, j) tries every split k; in burst balloons, k is the LAST balloon burst.
table: f(r, c) over right/down moves, count or min/max path sum
f(r, c) = 1 + min of three neighbors
f(i, j) over splits: matrix chain, burst balloons, cut stick, strange printer
f(i, j) = score difference the mover can force

files.desc: Unique paths, min path sum, triangle, maximal square, dungeon, cherry pickup II, burst balloons, matrix chain, cut stick, palindrome cuts, strange printer, stone game

pitfalls: Dungeon must run backward: the minimum health needed depends on what comes AFTER.
Burst balloons: think "last to burst" so the two sides become independent.
Pad the array with sentinels (1 at both ends) instead of special-casing borders.

views.title: Bitmask & Digit DP
views.intro: Bitmask memo f(mask) when n <= 20 and each item is used once. Digit memo f(pos, tight, started, property) when counting numbers up to N with a digit property.
table: Each worker takes one task, position = popcount(mask)
Fill buckets, track sum mod target
Memoize on the set of numbers taken
Count x in [0, N] with a property

files.desc: Assignment, k equal subsets, beautiful arrangement, can I win, digit one count, digit set, repeated digits

pitfalls: Digit dp: `tight` is only true while every prefix digit equals the bound; `started` handles leading zeros.
Subset enumeration `sub = (sub - 1) & mask` totals 3^n across all masks.
Use Integer.bitCount(mask) as the implicit "how many placed" index.

views.title: DP + Other Structures
views.intro: The hard-round combinations: memo with binary search (job scheduling), memo over a window of next indices (jump game VI), probability memo, hash-map state, and memoized DFS on an implicit DAG.
table: Weighted job scheduling: skip, or take and jump to the next compatible job
f(i) = nums[i] + best f(j) for j in the next k
O(nk); a monotonic deque gives O(n)
Distribution over states after k steps
Longest increasing path in a grid

files.desc: Job scheduling, constrained subset sum, jump game VI, knight probability, new 21 game, arithmetic subsequence, longest increasing path

pitfalls: Memo over a sliding window is O(nk); if that times out, the follow-up is a monotonic deque, which is not top-down.
Longest increasing path needs no visited set: strictly increasing values make the graph a DAG.

views.title: DP: Hard Variants
views.intro: Hard DP adds an extra dimension to a known shape: attached count (remove boxes), pile count (merge stones), two walkers (cherry pickup), difference as state (tallest billboard), or flipping the question (egg drop).
table: Remove boxes, merge stones, palindromic subsequences: f(l, r, extra)
f(eggs, floors) with binary search on the drop
Supersequence, divisible subset: walk the memo

files.desc: Frog jump, stone game II, predict the winner, super egg drop, dice rolls to target, paint house II, cherry pickup, out of boundary paths, domino tiling, distinct palindromic subsequences, profitable schemes, tallest billboard, best team score, remove boxes, merge stones, min cost tree from leaf values, shortest common supersequence, minimum insertions, three non-overlapping subarrays, delete and earn, integer break, divisible subset, string chain, vowel permutations, attendance record

pitfalls: State the dimension you added and what it stands for before writing the recurrence.
Interval DP with an extra state: memoize with the extra dimension, not just (l, r).
Reconstruction: walk the memo from the answer state, at each step taking the transition that produced the stored value; never recompute from scratch.

decisions.q: Count ways / min cost where step i reads a few earlier steps?
decisions.a: Memo over i: f(i) reads f(i-1), f(i-2)
Memo f(i) = max(take a[i] + f(i+2), skip f(i+1))
Memo best subarray starting at i (track max AND min for products)

decisions.q: Buy / sell with limits, cooldown or fee?
decisions.a: Memo over (day, holding, transactions left)

decisions.q: Choose a subset under a capacity, each item once?
decisions.a: Memo f(i, cap): skip item i, or take it once and move to i+1
Memo f(amount) = 1 + min over coins of f(amount - coin)
Combinations: memo f(coin index, amount); sequences: memo f(amount) trying every coin

decisions.q: Can the array be split into equal halves / signs assigned to hit a target?
decisions.a: Subset-sum reduction, then memo f(i, remaining)
Memo f(i) = LIS starting at i; answer = max over i
Memo f(i, j) over the two string suffixes
Memo f(i, j); star means skip it or consume one char

decisions.q: Can the string be segmented into dictionary words?
decisions.a: Memo f(start): can s[start..] be segmented?
Memo f(r, c) over right/down moves

decisions.q: Answer for range [i, j] from splitting at k?
decisions.a: Memo f(i, j) trying every split k (k = last to burst)
Memo f(mask) over the set already used

decisions.q: Count numbers up to N with a digit property?
decisions.a: Memo f(pos, tight, started, property) over digits

decisions.q: Best choice among the next k indices?
decisions.a: Memo f(i) over the next k indices

decisions.q: Intervals with weights, pick a compatible set?
decisions.a: Memo f(i) = skip job i, or take it and jump to the next compatible job

decisions.q: Interval DP where equal items attach to a group?
decisions.a: Memo f(l, r, k) with k equal boxes attached on the left
Memo f(i, j, piles)
Memo f(step, row1, row2) for both walkers at once
Memo f(i, difference) = best height of the shorter side
Memo f(eggs, floors), binary search the drop floor

decisions.q: Return the actual supersequence, not just its length?
decisions.a: Memo LCS f(i, j), then walk the memo to merge
Memo f(i, j), subtract the double-counted inner palindromes

calibration: SDE2 bar: climbing stairs, house robber, coin change, LIS, LCS, edit distance, unique paths, word break — say the state, the choice and the base case out loud, then write the memoized recursion.
SDE3 bar: knapsack variants (move to i + 1 vs stay at i), interval memo (burst balloons), bitmask memo, stock state machines, regex/wildcard matching, and reconstructing the answer from the memo.

Staff bar (for context): digit memo, memo + binary search, knowing when an O(nk) memo needs a deque follow-up, proving a greedy fails and DP is needed, and estimating state-space size and recursion depth.
Staff bar: explain the extra state and prove the transition is exhaustive; reconstruct the answer, not only its value.
